6. // A memory region is a contiguous, non-wrapping half-open byte interval of the

15. // (defined in `page.spec.rs`, `pub uninterp spec fn spec_addr<T: Address>`),
16. // exactly as `PageAligned<T>` does. Using `spec_addr` — rather than a
17. // `T: View<V = int>` bound on the `View` impl — is what lets the `View` (and the

19. // address-family `View` impls are all `cfg(verus_keep_ghost)`-gated and the

30. // Abstract value of a memory region: the geometry `(start, size)` (in bytes,
31. // as mathematical integers) plus the three metadata tags callers observe.
32. pub struct MemoryRegionView {
33.     /// First valid byte address of the region. Equals the `start` supplied at
34.     /// construction; for the truncated variant it is page-aligned. Also the
35.     /// `Ord` key for both region types.
36.     pub start: int,
37.     /// Length of the region in bytes. The interval is `[start, start + size)`.
38.     /// For the truncated variant it is a multiple of the page size.
39.     pub size: int,
40.     /// Classification of the region (Usable / Reserved / Mmio / Bad).
41.     pub typ: MemoryRegionType,
42.     /// Access permissions granted over the region.
43.     pub perm: AccessPermission,
44.     /// Optional MMIO caching policy; `None` for non-MMIO regions.
45.     pub cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>,

48. impl MemoryRegionView {
49.     /// Non-empty, non-wrapping interval lying within the address space. This is
50.     /// the geometry every constructed region guarantees and that caller
51.     /// arithmetic (`size - 1`, `start + size - 1`, `size / FRAME_SIZE`) relies
52.     /// on: `size >= 1` (`new` rejects `size == 0`) and the inclusive end
53.     /// `start + size - 1` never overflows the widest address representation.
54.     pub open spec fn wf_geometry(self) -> bool {
55.         &&& self.size >= 1
56.         &&& self.start >= 0
57.         &&& self.start + self.size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
58.     }
59. 
60.     /// Exclusive end of the half-open interval `[start, end)`.
61.     pub open spec fn spec_end(self) -> int {
62.         self.start + self.size
63.     }
64. 
65.     /// Inclusive last byte address (callers compute `start + size - 1`).
66.     pub open spec fn spec_last(self) -> int {
67.         self.start + self.size - 1
68.     }

70.     /// Whether `addr` lies in `[start, start + size)`.
71.     pub open spec fn contains(self, addr: int) -> bool {
72.         self.start <= addr < self.start + self.size
73.     }

76.     /// policy changes; geometry and the other tags are preserved (`..self`).
77.     pub open spec fn spec_set_cache_policy(self, policy: MmioCachePolicy) -> MemoryRegionView {
78.         MemoryRegionView { cache_policy: Some(policy), ..self }

83. // `closed`: callers reference `self@.start` / `self@.size` but the field-to-
84. // storage mapping (and the `spec_addr` projection of the typed `start`) does not
85. // leak. Unconditional over `T: Address` (see module comment).

103.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
104. 
105.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView {
106.         self.0@
107.     }
108. }

110. // Well-formedness of a base memory region: non-empty, non-wrapping geometry.
111. impl<T: Address> MemoryRegion<T> {
112.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
113.         self@.wf_geometry()
114.     }
115. }
116. 
117. // Well-formedness of a truncated region: base geometry plus page alignment of
118. // both endpoints (established by `TruncatedMemoryRegion::new`'s `align_up`), so
119. // `size / FRAME_SIZE` is exact and `start` needs no re-alignment.
120. impl<T: Address> TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
121.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
122.         &&& self@.wf_geometry()
123.         &&& self@.start % spec_page_size() == 0

159.     pub fn new(
160.         name: &str,
161.         start: T,
162.         size: usize,
163.         typ: MemoryRegionType,
164.         perm: AccessPermission,
165.     ) -> Result<Self, Error> {
166.         // Check if name is too long (byte length).
167.         if name.len() > Self::MEMORY_REGION_NAME_MAX {
168.             let reason: &str = "memory region name is too long";
169.             error!("{reason} (name.len={}, NAME_MAX={})", name.len(), Self::MEMORY_REGION_NAME_MAX);
170.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
171.         }
172. 
173.         // Check if size of the memory region is valid.
174.         if size == 0 {
175.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, "invalid memory region size"));
176.         }
177. 
178.         // Check if memory region is too big.
179.         let start_raw_addr: usize = start.clone().into_raw_value();
180.         let end_raw_addr: usize = match start_raw_addr.checked_add(size - 1) {
181.             Some(end_raw_addr) => end_raw_addr,
182.             None => {
183.                 return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::TooBig, "memory region is too big"));
184.             },
185.         };
186. 
187.         // Check if memory region spans outside the address space.
188.         if end_raw_addr > T::max_addr() {
189.             return Err(Error::new(
190.                 ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
191.                 "memory region spans outside the address space",
192.             ));
193.         }

195.         Ok(Self {
196.             name: name.to_string(),
197.             start,
198.             size,
199.             typ,
200.             perm,
201.             cache_policy: None,
202.         })

213.             // as the stored `start` (`spec_addr(&result) == self@.start`). `T` is

215.             // through the universal `spec_addr`, not `result@`. `Address: Copy`,

347.     /// - `size`: Size of the region in bytes (rounded up to page alignment).

349.     /// - `cache_policy`: Caching policy that controls PWT/PCD bits in page table entries.

357.         name: &str,
358.         start: PageAligned<T>,
359.         size: usize,
360.         perm: AccessPermission,
361.         cache_policy: MmioCachePolicy,
362.     ) -> Result<Self, Error> {

277.   **Excluded.**

280.   `start + size`; storing both invites an extra consistency clause in `inv()`.
281.   Callers want *both* numbers, but only one is primitive state — `end` is a

291.   Rust type already distinguishes them; encoding it in the shared View would be
292.   a type-system fact restated as spec state (an anti-pattern) and unused by any
293.   caller. **Excluded.**
294. 
295. - **`internal_inv()` mirroring private fields** — there is no internal
296.   bookkeeping beyond the five abstract fields; the only "hidden" structure is
297.   the wrapper nesting, which is a `closed view()` concern, not an invariant.
298.   No separate internal invariant is warranted. **Excluded.**
299.

310. | **No code-as-spec** | View states *what* a region is (an interval + tags), not *how* it is stored or truncated. ✅ |
311.

 ```rust
 // (Proposed as a reusable helper on the View — see "Spec Helpers" below.)
 //   non-empty:  size >= 1                (new rejects size == 0)
 //   no-wrap:    start >= 0 && start + size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
 //               (the interval fits the address space; start + size - 1 never
 //                overflows, so inclusive-end / frame-range math is well-defined)
 
 impl<T: Address + View<V = int>> MemoryRegion<T> {
     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
         self@.wf_geometry()
     }
 }
 
 impl<T: Address + View<V = int>> TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
         &&& self@.wf_geometry()                       // size >= 1, no wrap
         &&& self@.start % spec_page_size() == 0       // page-aligned start
         &&& self@.size  % spec_page_size() == 0       // page-multiple size
     }
 }
 ```
 
 Notes:
 - The no-wrap bound is stated abstractly against `usize::MAX` (the widest
   address representation). The concrete `T::max_addr()` bound enforced by `new`
   is *stronger*; the View only needs the weaker no-wrap fact because that is all
   caller arithmetic relies on, and it keeps the invariant `T`-agnostic.
 - **Implemented as designed.** Both `MemoryRegion::inv` (`wf_geometry()`) and the
   strengthened `TruncatedMemoryRegion::inv` (`wf_geometry()` + page alignment) are
   in `region.spec.rs`. Adding `wf_geometry` caused no proof churn: `inv()` is an
   `open spec fn` referenced by no in-scope contract, so it imposes no obligation
   on the four accessors (it documents the abstract well-formedness for callers
   and future phases). `wf_geometry`, `spec_end`, `spec_last`, `contains`, and the
   `spec_set_cache_policy` transition are all present as View helpers.
 
 ---
 
 ## Spec Helpers (on the View type)
 
 Per the skill, reusable spec logic lives on the View, not as extra `pub spec
 fn`s on the region impls. These encode exactly the derived quantities callers
 compute, so later `ensures` can hand them back directly.
 
 ```rust
 impl MemoryRegionView {
     /// Non-empty, non-wrapping interval within the address space.
     pub open spec fn wf_geometry(self) -> bool {
         &&& self.size >= 1
         &&& self.start >= 0
         &&& self.start + self.size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
     }
 
     /// Exclusive end of the half-open interval [start, end).
     pub open spec fn spec_end(self) -> int { self.start + self.size }
 
     /// Inclusive last byte address (callers compute `start + size - 1`).
     pub open spec fn spec_last(self) -> int { self.start + self.size - 1 }
 
     /// Whether `addr` lies in [start, start + size).
     pub open spec fn contains(self, addr: int) -> bool {
         self.start <= addr < self.start + self.size
     }
 }
 ```
 
 These are optional conveniences for downstream phases; the four target
 accessors themselves only need `result@ == self@.start` / `result == self@.size`
 style `ensures`. They are listed so spec authors reuse one definition of
 "inclusive end" / "contains" instead of re-deriving overflow-prone arithmetic.
 
 ---
 
 ## Spec Transition Functions
 
 The region types are almost entirely immutable. The **only** state-mutating
 exec function in the module is `MemoryRegion::set_cache_policy`, so it gets the
 sole transition (it is out of the current four-function scope but belongs to the
 View design for completeness):
 
 ```rust
 impl MemoryRegionView {
     pub open spec fn spec_set_cache_policy(self, policy: MmioCachePolicy) -> MemoryRegionView {
         MemoryRegionView { cache_policy: Some(policy), ..self }   // frame: geometry + tags preserved
     }
 }
 // ensures self@ == old(self)@.spec_set_cache_policy(policy)
 ```
 
 `..self` is the frame condition: `start`, `size`, `typ`, `perm` are unchanged.
 
 The constructors (`MemoryRegion::new`, `TruncatedMemoryRegion::new`,
 `new_mmio`, `from_memory_region`, `from_virtual_memory_region`) are *creation*,
 not `self`-transitions; they will be specified in later phases by stating the
 resulting `self@` (e.g. `result@.start == start@`, `result@.size` rounded up to
 a page multiple for the truncated path) rather than via a transition on an
 existing View. No transition function is owed for them here.
 
 The four in-scope accessors are pure reads — no transition, just `ensures`
 linking the return value to the View field. Because the return types (`T`,
 `PageAligned<T>`) are bare `Address` values (no `View` bound in the exec impl),
 the returned address is projected through `spec_addr`, not `result@`:
 
 | Function | Implemented ensures |
 |----------|----------------------------|
 | `MemoryRegion::start`            | `spec_addr(&result) == self@.start` |
 | `MemoryRegion::size`             | `result as int == self@.size`   |
 | `TruncatedMemoryRegion::start`   | `spec_addr(&result) == self@.start` (page alignment of `self@.start` follows from `self.inv()`) |
 | `TruncatedMemoryRegion::size`    | `result as int == self@.size`   |
 
 `TruncatedMemoryRegion::start` delegates to `MemoryRegion::start`; the forwarding
 `view()` (`self@ == self.0@`) makes `spec_addr(&result) == self.0@.start ==
 self@.start` discharge by delegation. `MemoryRegion::start` itself carries a
 specification-phase `admit()` placeholder: relating `spec_addr(&self.start.clone())`
 to `spec_addr(&self.start)` needs a value-preserving clone spec on the `Address`
 family, which is supplied in the proving phase.
 
 ---
 
 ## Design Rationale (per field, substitution test)
 
 > Substitution test: *if the implementation were completely rewritten with a
 > different algorithm, would this field still make sense?*
 
 | Field | Caller-observable via | Substitution test | Verdict |
 |-------|-----------------------|--------------------|---------|
 | `start: int` | `start()` (10 ext. sites: frame number, raw value, identity-map base, overlap key, Ord key) | Any region representation must expose a first address; callers read it as a frame/page base and as the ordering key. Independent of how it is stored (`T` vs `PageAligned<T>`). | ✅ keep |
 | `size: int` | `size()` (8 ext. sites: `size - 1`, `size / FRAME_SIZE`, region end, identity-map end) | Any representation must expose a byte length; callers do exact frame division and inclusive-end math. Survives any storage/truncation strategy. | ✅ keep |
 | `typ: MemoryRegionType` | `typ()` (14 refs) — routing/classification of regions | The classification is intrinsic region state, not an implementation artifact; survives a rewrite. Needed so `typ()` can later be specified. | ✅ keep |
 | `perm: AccessPermission` | `perm()` — permissions consumed when mapping | Intrinsic region attribute, independent of layout. | ✅ keep |
 | `cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>` | `cache_policy()` / mutated by `set_cache_policy()` | Intrinsic MMIO attribute and the target of the module's only mutator; the transition spec needs it. | ✅ keep |
 
 Abstract-type choices: `int` for `start`/`size` (not `usize`/`T`) so spec
 arithmetic — inclusive end, frame ranges, overlap — is overflow-free and matches
 how every caller uses the values (`into_raw_value()` then integer math). `Option`
 mirrors the optional cache policy. `typ`/`perm` are small `Copy` enums/structs
 carried as-is; abstracting them further would add no caller value.
 
 Shared View for both region types: the truncated variant *is* the same interval
 with a stronger invariant, and its `view()` forwards to the inner region. One
 View + a stronger `inv()` is simpler than two near-identical View types and lets
 callers (e.g. `MmioRegion::base`/`size`, the mmio allocator) reason uniformly.
 
 `view()` closed / `inv()` open: `closed` hides the field→storage mapping (e.g.
 that truncated regions wrap `MemoryRegion<PageAligned<T>>`); `open` `inv()`
 exposes the page-alignment and geometry facts callers must rely on
 (`size / FRAME_SIZE` exact, `start` needs no re-alignment).
 
 ---
 
 ## Rejected Alternatives
 
 - **`name: String` field** — `name()` is a public accessor, but the caller
   analysis explicitly states callers "don't care about" the name for any
   geometry/booking use, and no in-scope spec references it. Including it fails
   *minimality* (no spec uses it) without aiding any caller. It is display /
   identity metadata; if `name()` is ever brought into scope, add a
   `name: Seq<char>` field then. **Excluded.**
 
 - **`start: T` / `start: PageAligned<T>` (machine/typed address)** — mirrors the
   implementation field and forces callers to unwrap before doing arithmetic.
   Fails the abstract-type rule. The `int` abstraction (via `T::view() == int`)
   is what every caller actually computes on. **Excluded.**
 
 - **`size: usize` / `nat`** — `usize` re-introduces overflow into specs;
   `nat` would block expressing the no-wrap bound against `usize::MAX as int`
   cleanly and complicates `size - 1` reasoning. `int` is the right spec type.
   **Excluded.**
 
 - **`end: int` as a stored field (instead of `size`)** — redundant with
   `start + size`; storing both invites an extra consistency clause in `inv()`.
   Callers want *both* numbers, but only one is primitive state — `end` is a
   derived helper (`spec_end`), not a field. **Excluded as a field; kept as a
   helper.**
 
 - **A separate `TruncatedMemoryRegionView`** — would duplicate all five fields
   to add nothing but the page-alignment facts, which belong in `inv()` not in a
   new struct. The `closed` forwarding `view()` already gives the truncated type
   its own abstraction surface. **Excluded.**
 
 - **`is_truncated: bool` / a tag distinguishing the two region kinds** — the
   Rust type already distinguishes them; encoding it in the shared View would be
   a type-system fact restated as spec state (an anti-pattern) and unused by any
   caller. **Excluded.**
 
 - **`internal_inv()` mirroring private fields** — there is no internal
   bookkeeping beyond the five abstract fields; the only "hidden" structure is
   the wrapper nesting, which is a `closed view()` concern, not an invariant.
   No separate internal invariant is warranted. **Excluded.**
 
 ---
 
 ## Quality Review
 
 | Criterion | Check |
 |-----------|-------|
 | **Substitution** | All five fields describe intrinsic region state surviving any rewrite. ✅ |
 | **Caller-only** | Every field is exposed by a public accessor and used by real callers (geometry by the four targets; tags by `typ`/`perm`/`cache_policy`). ✅ |
 | **Complete** | `(start, size)` + tags cover every caller-observable concept in the analysis (frame math, overlap, Ord key, routing, MMIO policy). ✅ |
 | **Minimal** | No unused field — `name` deliberately omitted. Each field maps to ≥1 (current or near-term) spec. ✅ |
 | **No code-as-spec** | View states *what* a region is (an interval + tags), not *how* it is stored or truncated. ✅ |

name: ast-consistency
description: "AST-level exec fidelity checking tools and pre-approved deviations. Use after modifying source files to verify exec code is unchanged."

# AST Consistency Check

Source exec code must not change during verification — see `verus-constraints`
for the full rules. This skill covers the **tooling** to enforce that guarantee.

## Tools

The checker uses tree-sitter to hash exec code after stripping all
ghost/proof/spec annotations. It detects changes invisible to textual diff.

`scripts/ast_consistency.py` provides four subcommands:
- `count` — quick pass/fail
- `summary` — per-element status table
- `diff --name "Fn::name"` — unified diff for one function/struct
- `report -o <dir>` — full report with all diffs

The `source` argument is optional. Use `--base-ref` to extract the original
from git, or omit both on `verus-ai/*` branches for auto-detection:

```bash
# Explicit original file:
python3 scripts/ast_consistency.py original.rs verified.rs count

# Via git ref:
python3 scripts/ast_consistency.py --base-ref main verified.rs count

# Auto-detect on verus-ai/* branches:
python3 scripts/ast_consistency.py verified.rs count
```

`diff` with `--full` shows specs; default is exec-only.

**MCP alternative**: If the `verus-ast` MCP server is registered, the same
functionality is available as tools (`ast_count`, `ast_summary`, `ast_diff`,
`ast_report`) with the same auto-detection.

## Pre-Approved Deviations

These minimal exec changes are known Verus limitations — no full deviation
process needed, but still document with a comment:

| Original | Verus Version | Reason |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `self.x += 1` | `self.x = self.x + 1` | Compound assignment unsupported |
| `self.arr[i] \|= v` | `self.arr.set(i, self.arr[i] \| v)` | Mutable index unsupported |
| `-> T` | `-> (ret: T)` | Named returns for ensures |
| `#[derive(Clone, ...)]` | `#[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))] #[derive(...)]` | cfg-gating incompatible derives |
| `Ok(Self { .. })` | `let result = Self { .. }; Ok(result)` | Ensures needs to reference return value |
| `f(complex_expr)` | `let x = complex_expr; f(x)` | Intermediate value for assertions |
| `.ok_or_else(\|\| ...)` | `match ... { Some(v) => v, None => return Err(...) }` | Closures unsupported in some contexts |
| `v.std_method(args)` | `wrapper(&mut v, args)` | `&mut T` method unsupported; see `verus-constraints` skill for wrapper rules |

### Bug Fix Deviations

Exec changes that fix verified bugs are also pre-approved. These must:
- Have a `// VERUS BUG FIX: <description>` comment at the fix site
- Be recorded in `bugs.md` with full evidence
- Be committed with `[verus-ai] BUG FIX:` prefix
- Be limited to auto-fixable categories (overflow, off-by-one, missing
  bounds check, unchecked cast) — see `bug-reporting` skill

## Handling MISMATCHes

When the checker reports a MISMATCH:

1. **Default: restore original code.** Exec changes are violations. Use
   `git show <base_ref>:path/to/file.rs` to view the original, then
   manually restore the changed exec code while keeping your annotations.
   Adapt the proof to the original code — not the other way around.
2. **Check pre-approved deviations.** If the change matches one above,
   keep it but add a comment documenting which deviation and why.
3. **Verify it's a real Verus limitation.** Before accepting any other
   change, confirm Verus genuinely cannot handle the original construct:
   - Search vstd for existing support (e.g. `checked_mul` has vstd specs)
   - Try alternative proof strategies that preserve the original code
   - Build a minimal reproducer proving the limitation
4. **If confirmed, document with full evidence.** Add a `VERUS DEVIATION`
   comment explaining: what was changed, why the original doesn't work,
   what alternatives were tried, and why this is the smallest possible change.
